url_citation.title: First City Takes Off as Georgia's Newest Bank
url_citation.content:
Let’s talk about Georgia’s newest bank.

Bob Koncerak thought he was done with banking.
More than a decade ago, he chronicled the post-crisis roller coaster of community banking in his book, The Most Fun I Never Want to Have Again: A Midlife Crisis in Community Banking . He even joked that if he ever wrote a sequel, he might call it I Thought I Was Done the Last Time .
Turns out, he wasn’t done.
Koncerak is now president and CEO of the newly rebranded First City Bank in Alpharetta, Ga., where he and his team raised more than $22 million, bought the state’s smallest bank, and brought a fresh community banking model to one of metro Atlanta’s most dynamic markets.
We caught up with Koncerak to discuss why he came back, what the capital raise says about the staying power of community banking, how technology has changed the de novo process, and why First City is betting on local relationships, commercial customers, and experienced bankers.
Here’s an edited transcript.

I remember reading your book. Really enjoyed it. Then you seemed to be off the grid. What led you to get back in the game?

BOB KONCERAK: The very last line of that book said, ‘If I ever go do this again, I’m going to title the book I thought I was done the last time.’ It’s been quite a ride in what I refer to as my so-called career.

Mary Ellen Biery
September 9, 2013
0 min read

Bob Koncerak, who has nearly 30 years of experience in financial services and corporate finance, is the author of a new book that gives an insider’s perspective on Georgia’s community banking industry during the boom years up to 2007 and through the U.S. financial crisis and its aftermath. The Most Fun I Never Want To Have Again: A Mid-life Crisis In Community Banking is part history, part leadership and business advice. In the excerpt that follows, Koncerak describes the environment as he began to help develop a new banking enterprise, Touchmark National Bank, during this historic time period.
Koncerak is currently engaged as executive vice president and chief financial officer for a multi-bank holding company in Alabama, and he is principal at BankForward Consulting, LLC. He has held both managerial and executive positions throughout his career, including Capital Markets CFO at the former Wachovia Bank, and the executive vice president/CFO for the “de novo” launch of Touchmark National Bank. Koncerak lives in Alpharetta, Ga.
